title: Kongnamul Guk
subtitle: Clear bean sprout soup
excerpt: A light, clean Korean soup built on bean sprouts, garlic, and a touch of sesame. It comes together in under twenty minutes and is a staple on the Korean table alongside rice and banchan. The broth is delicate but full of flavour.
sourceNotes: Kongnamul guk is one of the most widely eaten soups in Korea, appearing daily on home tables across the country. It is particularly associated with hangover recovery and is often served at breakfast the morning after celebrations, prized for its clean, restorative broth.

glossaryTerms.definition: Kongnamul is the Korean word for soybean sprouts, which are slightly thicker and more robust than mung bean sprouts. They are a fundamental ingredient in Korean cooking, used in soups, stir-fries, and seasoned side dishes. Their slightly nutty flavour and satisfying crunch make them one of the most versatile vegetables in the Korean pantry.

Doenjang is a fermented Korean soybean paste with a deep, savoury, slightly funky flavour. It is similar in role to Japanese miso but has a coarser texture and a more pungent taste. A spoonful stirred into a clear soup or stew adds considerable body and complexity.

content.text: This soup serves 4 and is ready in about 20 minutes from start to finish. It is built on
, soybean sprouts that cook quickly in a simple broth of water, garlic, and a splash of soy sauce. The result is a clean, restorative soup that pairs with steamed rice at almost any meal.
This recipe uses soy sauce to keep it fully vegan. If you want a more savoury depth, stir in half a teaspoon of

at the end of cooking. Fish sauce is traditional in many households and adds another layer of flavour, but it takes the soup outside vegan territory. Avoid overcooking the sprouts: they should be tender but still have a slight bite.

items.prepNote: optional, for colour and mild heat

content.text: Bring 1 litre of water to the boil in a medium saucepan.
Add the garlic and soy sauce. Stir briefly and reduce the heat to a steady simmer.
Add the bean sprouts. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes until the sprouts are just tender but not mushy.
Add the spring onions and gochugaru if using. Cook for a further 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning with a little more soy sauce if needed. Serve immediately with steamed rice.

items.cause: Soy sauce alone can lack depth without a proper stock base
items.fix: Stir in half a teaspoon of doenjang or a splash of fish sauce and simmer for 2 more minutes before serving
Add the sprouts for no more than 10 minutes total. They continue to soften in the residual heat, so pull them just before they reach the texture you want

items.cause: Soy sauce varies considerably in saltiness between brands
items.fix: Add a splash of water to dilute, then taste again. Start with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and adjust upward at the end

content.text: Kongnamul guk is a soup that shows up on Korean tables every day of the week. It is part of the structure of a Korean meal rather than a centrepiece dish. Koreans eat it alongside rice, kimchi, and other small side dishes. It is one of the first soups many Korean children grow up eating. It is also a classic hangover remedy, valued for its clean broth and gentle seasoning. It costs almost nothing to make and takes minimal effort. The simplicity is the point.
